details:
Amplify Vision: A NASA-Inspired Space Mission Engineering and Exploration Simulator

Amplify Vision is an interactive, NASA-resource-informed space mission engineering and exploration simulator designed to make complex space engineering concepts accessible through hands-on learning and experimentation. It allows users to experience the complete mission lifecycle, from defining scientific objectives and designing spacecraft to selecting launch vehicles, planning planetary missions, managing spacecraft resources, and evaluating mission outcomes.

The platform features two primary modes: Mission Mode, which offers 27 structured missions with specific objectives and engineering constraints, and Freeplay Mode, which allows users to independently design and experiment with spacecraft configurations and mission scenarios.

Users can build spacecraft using different propulsion systems, solar panels, communication systems, scientific instruments, and payloads. The simulator calculates parameters such as mass, power consumption, power margins, estimated delta-v, mission costs, and scientific capabilities, helping users understand the trade-offs involved in real-world mission engineering. Following spacecraft configuration, users can select launch vehicles, experience interactive 3D launch sequences, and explore planetary destinations.

A dedicated Mission Control environment extends the experience beyond launch. Users can monitor simulated spacecraft telemetry, manage battery and power consumption, schedule scientific observations, operate instruments, collect science data, and manage communication windows and data downlinks. The platform also supports collaborative mission operations, allowing up to four participants to work together through shared mission sessions and assigned team roles.

A key feature is its integration of real scientific resources from NASA, NASA/JPL, NOAA, and USGS. These include NASA/JPL Horizons planetary and spacecraft ephemeris data, NASA mission imagery, Earth observation datasets, NOAA space weather forecasts, NASA EONET natural-event records, and asteroid close-approach information from JPL. The dedicated Juno simulation uses JPL Horizons spacecraft vectors to visualize its position relative to Jupiter. These integrations connect the educational experience with authentic scientific datasets while clearly distinguishing real agency information from simplified gameplay models.

Technology and Development Tools: The application was developed using React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Three.js, and React Three Fiber. Node.js powers the backend API infrastructure, while browser local storage maintains campaign progress and mission sessions. NASA spacecraft models are integrated using GLTF/GLB and STL formats. External data integrations use official public APIs, including NASA Images, JPL Horizons, NASA EPIC, NASA GIBS, NASA EONET, NOAA SWPC, and USGS LandsatLook. Groq provides the optional AI-powered NASA Mission Control educational assistant, which can discover and retrieve relevant NASA Earthdata resources through NASA's Earthdata Common Metadata Repository MCP service.

Innovation and Creativity: Amplify Vision brings spacecraft design, engineering calculations, 3D visualization, planetary exploration, scientific observations, resource management, and collaborative mission operations together in a unified interactive experience. Rather than presenting space science as static educational material, it allows learners to make engineering decisions, observe their consequences, encounter mission constraints, and improve their designs through experimentation. Its combination of authentic scientific data, locally integrated NASA 3D assets, interactive simulations, and AI-assisted scientific exploration creates an engaging approach to learning space engineering.

Intended Impact: The project aims to make space science and engineering education more accessible, particularly for students and educational institutions with limited access to specialized laboratories, expensive simulation software, or practical aerospace learning opportunities. By providing a browser-based environment for experimentation, it encourages STEM education, computational thinking, engineering problem-solving, scientific curiosity, and collaborative learning. Ultimately, Amplify Vision aims to help students move beyond simply learning about space missions to understanding how they are designed, managed, and operated.
